Materials and methods WSI-Babel-Shark integrates data matrix code decoding, region of interest (ROI)-based optical character recognition (OCR), and rule-based metadata parsing within a modular Python and Docker architecture. To handle diverse institutional label formats, the system incorporates a deep learning-based label layout classifier using a ResNet-18 backbone, fused with handcrafted descriptors and prototype-based open-set recognition to categorize labels into 10 predefined layout groups. A graphical interface supports ROI annotation, dataset management, and configuration editing. Performance was evaluated on 270 WSIs (.svs and .ndpi formats) and cross-validated using 110 slides from the previously published WSI-Babel-Fish dataset to assess backward compatibility. Results The label layout classifier achieved an overall accuracy of 97.4%, with macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.98 while reliably rejecting previously unseen layouts. End-to-end pipeline evaluation achieved complete SlideID reconstruction for 258 of 267 evaluable WSIs (96.6%). Independent comparison of OCR-derived metadata with the corresponding Data Matrix-decoded metadata on 236 slides demonstrated complete metadata concordance for 230 slides (97.5%), whereas field-level concordance ranged from 98.3% to 100.0% across all evaluated metadata fields. Cross-dataset analysis confirmed full compatibility with WSI-Babel-Fish label structures. Conclusion WSI-Babel-Shark advances automated metadata extraction from WSIs by introducing a label-layout classification framework validated on heterogeneous label layouts and incorporating open-set recognition, together with standardized ROI annotation and a fully containerized implementation. The framework ensures reproducible linkage between digitized slides and lab information, is designed to facilitate interoperability with lab information systems, and provides a scalable foundation for large-scale digital pathology workflows. The complete implementation is openly available at: https://github.com/cpheidelberg/WSI-Babel-Shark .

title: Knowledge-Interposed Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Supervisory Control Synthesis in Electric Flying Vehicles
abstract: Energy supervisory control (ESC) for electric flying vehicles is challenged by strong air–ground mode coupling and stringent safety constraints. Conventional reinforcement learning–based ESC typically requires extensive training and are difficult to bootstrap from scratch, which often leads to inefficient exploration and delayed satisfaction of safety constraints. To address this issue, we propose a large language model–enhanced curriculum learning warm start for soft actor–critic (CL-LSAC), which incorporates expert prior knowledge from large language models. The proposed curriculum prioritizes safety constraints before fuel efficiency, guiding policy learning through a highly non-convex reward landscape. Evaluated on a high-fidelity urban air mobility mission, CL-LSAC significantly suppresses the control saturation observed in unguided baselines. Compared with static reward weighting, our method improves state-of-charge regulation accuracy by 49% and accelerates convergence by more than 15% via LLM-guided initialization, yielding data-efficient and physically consistent policies that demonstrate high real-time execution feasibility on hardware-in-the-loop platforms.

title: H‐ SPDZ ‐Cloud: A Formal Prototype for Hierarchical Authenticated MPC in Edge–Fog–Cloud Architectures
abstract: ABSTRACT Hierarchical Edge–Fog–Cloud infrastructures increasingly support distributed sensing, analytics, and collaborative computation over sensitive data. Their multi‐tier structure creates systems challenges for secure orchestration: resources are heterogeneous, communication costs vary sharply across layers, and trust assumptions are often bounded by administrative domains. This paper presents H‐SPDZ‐Cloud, a formal prototype for hierarchical authenticated secure multi‐party computation over Edge–Fog–Cloud architectures. The design organizes computation into cryptographically isolated levels, each using an independent message authentication code key, and introduces a verified inter‐level resharing mechanism that keeps secrets in shared form during normal‐case upward transitions. The prototype also includes localized fault handling under a per‐level honest‐majority assumption suited to bounded hierarchical deployments. The H‐SPDZ‐Cloud prototype is evaluated in a controlled single‐host reproducibility testbed configured with the 127‐bit Mersenne prime field , represented using 16‐byte field‐element encodings. Prototype measurements show communication‐locality behavior relative to an internal flat SPDZ‐style Python baseline, with a 31.4% reduction in measured online communication and a 42.4% reduction in total communication for the tested workload. The prototype also evaluates secure fixed‐point inference on the public Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer dataset, with secret‐shared test features and 100% agreement between the secure and quantized plaintext predictions on the secured subset. The implemented 127‐bit‐prime‐field pipeline uses fixed‐base precomputation for the BN254/Pedersen transition evidence, the corrected masked batch MAC check, and a prototype Sigma/Schnorr dispute‐proof fallback, yielding a measured local‐pipeline latency of 696.2 ms and an fault‐localization latency of 3066.8 ms as reproducible prototype timings. TCP validation with independent party servers further exercises socket serialization and process‐isolated Edge/Fog transition workers; a subsequent authenticated multi‐region three‐VPS validation executes the external‐endpoint path from an independent Cloud controller to Edge and Fog VPS workers over TLS 1.3, reporting 229.2 ms mean TCP/TLS latency, 93.5 ms transition‐fault detection with 30/30 detections, and 264.3 ms/sample secure‐inference latency. A separate local MP‐SPDZ MASCOT reference execution confirms that the three reference arithmetic workloads also run in a standard MPC framework, while H‐SPDZ‐Cloud measurements use the Python prototype pipeline. The manuscript implements and measures an optimistic verification and pessimistic privacy‐preserving dispute path, with plaintext audit opening reserved for a separate administrative debug mode.

title: Bayesian Quantile Deep Echo State Networks for Nonlinear Time Series
abstract: Conditional quantiles are central to asymmetric decision losses, tail-risk assessment, and interval forecasts, but Bayesian quantile regression for nonlinear time series can be difficult when the temporal feature vector is high-dimensional. We develop the quantile deep echo state network (Q-DESN), a Bayesian quantile regression model conditional on fixed features generated by a deep echo state network. Conditional on a specified reservoir construction and feature map, posterior uncertainty is assigned to the regression coefficients, likelihood, and shrinkage parameters. Single-level fits use asymmetric Laplace or quantile-fixed generalized asymmetric Laplace working likelihoods with ridge or regularized-horseshoe priors. Posterior computation uses Markov chain Monte Carlo when computationally practical and a model-specific variational Bayes approximation for analyses requiring repeated fitting. For quantile grids, we compare independent level-wise regressions followed by monotone rearrangement with a joint quantile-vector regression that shrinks adjacent quantile-specific coefficient differences. Synthetic studies, a single-origin retrospective Global Flood Awareness System (GloFAS) streamflow case, and a retrospective PriceFM comparison identify settings where this fixed-feature Bayesian regression improves finite-grid quantile scores.

title: SPD: Single Pass Decoding for Generative Reranking
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve state-of-the-art generative ranking quality, but the ranking they produce must be decoded, and autoregressive decoding spends one sequential forward pass per emitted token. We observe that the only tokens a ranker must emit are the $N$ ordinal values naming the items in ranked order, and that this narrow, permutation-structured output format admits decoding strategies which are much more efficient than left-to-right generation. We introduce SPD (Single Forward Pass), a format-specialized decoding strategy that decodes all $N$ ordinals in $O(1)$ forward passes. SPD reads an $N \times K$ item-position score matrix off the LLM's prefill hidden states with a lightweight self-attention head, then decodes the ordinals as the optimal bipartite assignment of that matrix via the Hungarian algorithm, yielding a valid permutation by construction rather than by repair. Through a systematic study of training signals and backbone adaptation, we show that LoRA-based fine-tuning combined with auto-regressive LLM ranking distillation reaches 28 ms end-to-end inference, a speed-up of 64x while maintaining ranking quality on par with the teacher. We provide a complete ablation decomposing the contributions of architecture, training signal, and backbone adaptation. Our framework connects generative ranking to combinatorial optimization, opening a path toward other $O(1)$-decode mechanisms for real-time ranking.

title: Births are difficult to predict even with rich survey and full-population register data
abstract: Major life events have proven difficult to predict. Does this reflect limits of theory, data, and algorithms, or the large role of chance? We examine one outcome - having a child within three years - through a near-ideal setting for prediction: a data challenge where 147 researchers predicted births for Dutch residents aged 18-45, using survey data and full-population registers. Methods ranged from logistic regression to a large language model and transformers. Predictions were moderately accurate (best F1: register 0.59, survey 0.76); advanced models did not outperform classical ones; and the larger registers did not beat the survey. Simulating the stochastic biology of conception and pregnancy, we estimated a predictive ceiling (survey F1 ~ 0.86-0.94, register 0.88-0.96). Observed performance falls short of this ceiling, implicating imperfect data, methods, and unmodelled chance, while the ceiling itself shows that chance in reproduction alone sets a non-trivial limit on predicting individual lives.

title: Beyond the Image Plane: World-Grounded Queries for Multi-Object Tracking
abstract: Monocular videos record 3D scenes as sequences of 2D image-plane projections, obscuring depth and spatial relationships. Multi-object trackers localize and associate objects primarily using appearance and geometry observed only in the image plane, inheriting these ambiguities. To address this limitation, we introduce PLANET, an end-to-end multi-object tracker designed to move beyond the image plane. As an enabling step, we lift existing 2D tracking datasets into 3D. We then form world-grounded queries by embedding reconstructed 3D scene geometry into the features and positional encodings used during query formation. An auxiliary 3D location prediction task further encourages the queries to encode object positions during training. A complementary dual-resolution temporal memory preserves this evidence across longer temporal gaps. As a result, PLANET achieves state-of-the-art performance across three diverse benchmarks.

title: Efficient and Robust Absolute Pose Estimation via Gravity-Prior-Driven Transformation Decoupling and Pose Refinement
abstract: Estimation of the absolute pose of an object is an essential task for various robotic applications. Recently, incorporating gravity direction as prior information has emerged as a popular approach to simplify absolute pose estimation. However, developing a robust and efficient algorithm to solve this challenging problem remains a difficult question due to large amounts of mismatches. In addition, obtaining an accurate pose solution from selected inlier correspondences with gravity prior is still a research gap. In this paper, we propose a novel transformation strategy that exploits geometric relations derived from the gravity prior. Through transformation decoupling, the original 6 degrees of freedom (DoF) absolute pose estimation problem is simplified into a 4-DoFs problem: 1-DoF for the rotation angle and 3-DoFs for translation, significantly improving the efficiency. For the 1-DoF rotation angle, we apply a one-dimensional global voting algorithm for optimal estimation. Once the optimal rotation is obtained, the mismatched correspondences are preliminarily filtered, and translation estimation, a linear problem, can be easily solved. Furthermore, to obtain accurate pose results, we introduce a novel pose refinement algorithm to enhance the accuracy of both rotation and translation. Extensive experiments on synthetic data and three publicly available real-world datasets (TUM RGB-D, ETH3D, and RobotCar) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves stronger performance compared to existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches. To further validate our method, we integrated it into ORB-SLAM2. The results on the KITTI dataset show it effectively reduces drift and improves trajectory alignment during relocalization. The source code will be released upon acceptance.

title: Distribution-free fair federated learning with small samples
abstract: As federated learning gains increasing importance in real-world applications due to its capacity for decentralized data training, addressing fairness concerns across demographic groups becomes critically important. However, most existing machine learning algorithms for ensuring fairness are designed for centralized data environments and generally require large-sample and distributional assumptions, underscoring the urgent need for fairness techniques adapted for decentralized and heterogeneous systems with finite-sample and distribution-free guarantees. To address this issue, this paper introduces FedFaiREE, a post-processing algorithm developed specifically for distribution-free fair learning in decentralized settings with small samples. Our approach accounts for unique challenges in decentralized environments, such as client heterogeneity, communication costs, and small sample sizes. We provide rigorous theoretical guarantees for both fairness and accuracy, and our experimental results further provide robust empirical validation for our proposed method.

title: LiteNet: lightweight network traffic classification using explainable artificial intelligence and model compression
abstract: Background Network Traffic Classification (NTC) is a critical process in network management as it increases visibility to provide enhanced security, optimised resource allocation, and quality of service. However, the escalating volume of network traffic and real-time applications in modern networking is straining traditional processing on high-performance servers. To meet modern requirements for low latency and bandwidth efficiency, network management is increasingly moving computation closer to sources that generate the data, a paradigm referred to as edge computing. This shift relies on resource-constrained devices such as routers, switches, and embedded systems. To address these constraints, researchers proposed lightweight NTC models designed to operate effectively in such environments. However, while these methods offer greater efficiency, they often compromise performance, making the models less effective in practice. Furthermore, despite being lightweight, the throughput of current NTC models remains insufficient to keep up with the high bandwidth demands of modern networks, which continues to limit their practical deployment. Methods Therefore, this article proposes LiteNet, a lightweight model for real-time NTC in a resource-constrained environment to address the disparity between model complexity and edge device limitations. LiteNet adapts the InceptionV1 module that integrates four dedicated parallel branches. Additionally, we integrate DeepSHAP, an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) technique, to enhance explainability and reduce input features. Furthermore, we leverage model compression techniques, including semi-structured pruning and quantisation, to form a sparse LiteNet architecture that enables lightweight design and real-time classification. Results LiteNet demonstrated F1-scores exceeding 99% across two datasets, ISCXVPN2016 and MalayaNetwork_GT, while having 40% fewer parameters compared to the baseline method. Benchmarking results demonstrated that LiteNet outperformed the state-of-the-art method in terms of performance and efficiency, delivering up to 238% higher throughput and lower resource utilisation on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano. These outcomes demonstrate LiteNet’s strong balance between performance and efficiency, establishing it as a viable lightweight solution for NTC in resource-constrained settings.

title: SEMANTIC REASONING AND EXPLAINABLE PERSONALIZATION: A KNOWLEDGE GRAPH FRAMEWORK FOR REAL-TIME WORKPLACE PRODUCTIVITY ASSESSMENT
abstract: Individual productivity remains a critical determinant of both organizational success andemployee well-being, yet the factors driving it are inherently multifaceted and highly context-dependent. Contemporary productivity support systems frequently operate in silos monitoringenvironmental, physiological, or behavioural variables independently, which constrains theircapacity to deliver genuinely personalized and interpretable interventions tailored to individualcircumstances. This thesis presents PROD-TS, an adaptive Knowledge Graph-driven intelligentsystem designed to enhance workplace productivity through evidence-based recommendationsand gamified incentive mechanisms. The proposed framework unifies disparate data streamsspanning indoor environmental quality measurements (CO₂, thermal comfort, lighting), wearable-derived physiological indicators (heart rate, heart rate variability, stress markers), andpsychometric user profiles (BFI-10, NEP, IPAQ) into a cohesive semantic knowledgerepresentation, the TS-Knowledge Graph, formalized using RDF/OWL ontologies. A rule-basedreasoning layer (SWRL) semantically enriches the graph with machine-interpretable domainknowledge and synthesizes these heterogeneous signals into a unified Daily Productivity Score(DPS) reflecting individual capacity and performance potential. The enriched TS-KG issubsequently leveraged through a Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG)architecture to construct a rich Unified User Context, grounding a Large Language Model togenerate contextually appropriate behavioural nudges and adaptive gamified incentive strategies.Crucially, user interactions and feedback are continuously integrated back into the graph,establishing a closed-loop personalization cycle that refines recommendations over time. Thesystem was validated using synthetic multi-modal data from 25 simulated participants trackedover 90 days. Experimental findings demonstrate that knowledge-grounded LLMrecommendations consistently outperformed non-grounded baselines across perceived relevance,personalization depth, explainability, and user trust. These results underscore the value ofcombining formal semantic representation, graph-based reasoning, and generative AI for buildinghuman-centred, interpretable productivity support systems. Keywords: Knowledge Graph, TS-KG, GraphRAG, Large Language Models, WorkplaceProductivity, Semantic Reasoning, Rule-Based Reasoning, Indoor Environmental Quality,Physiological Monitoring, Personalized Recommendations, Gamification, Daily ProductivityScore, Explainability, User Trust

title: Deltakit/deltakit-compile: Release v0.1.0
abstract: Deltakit-compile deltakit-compile is a compiler implementation for Quantum Error Correction. This v0.1.0 release open-sources compiler intermediate representations, the Circuit-Builder and Logial-Assembly APIs, and compilation infrastructure developed internally at Riverlane as a package. This will enable the commuity of Deltakit users to develop new and interesting fault-toloerent quantum programs, QEC compilation tools, and software for quantum programing that is aware of real-time error correction. title: A Topological Approach to Artificial Intelligence: The 5D Metatron Reasoning Model (5D-MRM) with Topo-Adaptive Mutating Nodes
abstract: This framework introduces the 5D Metatron Reasoning Model (5D-MRM), a novel concept in Topological Deep Learning (TDL) and Geometric Deep Learning (GDL). While standard artificial intelligence structures operate on static multi-dimensional vector spaces, the 5D-MRM utilizes a 5-dimensional hyper-graph structure constrained by the structural symmetries of a 5D-expanded Metatron's Cube lattice. A core mechanic of this framework is the deployment of topo-adaptive mutating nodes. In this architecture, spatial mutation occurs dynamically at the second node of a reasoning sequence as a direct result of relational friction during chain formation. This interaction forces a topological phase transition and directional hyper-rotation along the 5th-dimensional evolutionary axis. The complete history of this structural mutation pathway down the chain collapses into a newly birthed 5-dimensional hypercube, which physically crystallizes the logical argument. This model addresses the stability-plasticity dilemma by maintaining a stable foundational core while isolating radical, real-time reasoning adjustments to the 5th-dimensional axis.

title: Epistemic Architecture v0.1: Conformance Specification and Test Suite
abstract: Epistemic Architecture v0.1 is a minimal formal specification for representing, governing, and testing epistemic state transitions in a constrained system. The release defines a small state architecture together with an explicit conformance specification and machine-readable test suite. It distinguishes permissible epistemic transitions from prohibited transitions and provides a reproducible basis for evaluating whether an implementation conforms to the stated architecture. The bundle contains: - "epistemic_architecture_v0.1.md" — the core architectural specification. - "EPI-CONFORMANCE-001_v0.1.yaml" — the machine-readable conformance test specification. - "README.md" — release and usage information. This release is intended as a minimal, auditable specification and conformance artifact, rather than as a claim that the underlying epistemic architecture is empirically established. Version: 0.1 Status: Experimental / specification release

title: Title: Adaptive Bayesian Network for Time Series Prediction with Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Bayesian Network (ABN) for time series prediction, focusing on enhancing predictive accuracy and providing robust uncertainty quantification. Traditional Bayesian networks struggle with dynamic uncertainty, necessitating iterative refinement. We propose a novel 'Bayesian adjustment' mechanism that dynamically updates the network's probabilistic weights based on observed data and uncertainty measures, enabling a more responsive and accurate prediction process. The system employs a Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) to guide the adjustment, ensuring a balance between prediction accuracy and uncertainty reduction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of benchmark time series datasets, showcasing significant improvements in both prediction performance and uncertainty estimation compared to existing methods. The results highlight the advantages of this adaptive approach in handling complex time series data with inherent uncertainty.

title: # Central American Red Brocket: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by a Novel Foraging Strategy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Central American Red Brocket" (CARB), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Central American Red Brocket ( *Dinura rufescens*). The algorithm mimics the observed strategies of this bird, particularly its adaptive search pattern and exploitation of local resources, to achieve efficient solution exploration and convergence in optimization problems. CARB employs a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a unique 'resource allocation' mechanism that dynamically adjusts the search space based on the perceived 'abundance' of potential solutions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark test functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling both continuous and discrete optimization challenges. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the search space, driven by a simulated 'resource scarcity' model, which promotes a balance between exploration and exploitation, ultimately leading to faster convergence and improved solution quality compared to traditional metaheuristics. The algorithm's parameters are tuned using a self-adaptive mechanism, further enhancing its robustness and adaptability to different problem landscapes. The results presented indicate that CARB offers a promising alternative for a wide range of optimization problems, particularly those exhibiting complex, multi-modal landscapes.

title: Quantum Entanglement Modeling: A Non-Asymmetric Framework for Enhanced Quantum Computing Reliability and Efficiency
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon with immense potential for quantum computation, yet its practical realization faces significant challenges related to decoherence and measurement. This paper explores a novel approach to modeling quantum entanglement, centered around the principle of non-asymmetry. We propose a framework that leverages non-symmetry to simplify entanglement descriptions and design algorithms to optimize entanglement stability and transmission. The core claim is that this framework significantly improves the reliability and efficiency of quantum computing through enhanced entanglement management.

title: Bush Elephant: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bush Elephant Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bush Elephant, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the foraging behavior of bush elephants, specifically their strategies for locating and exploiting food resources in challenging environments. Bush Elephant leverages a combination of adaptive memory, local search, and a novel convergence criterion based on the elephant's memory of successful foraging locations. The algorithm's core components include an adaptive memory system for storing promising solutions, a local search operator mimicking the elephant's exploration and exploitation phases, and a dynamically adjusted step size based on the perceived environmental complexity. The performance of Bush Elephant is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results show that Bush Elephant can outperform several established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. The algorithm's design emphasizes robustness and adaptability, making it suitable for a wide variety of applications. The key mathematical formulation and algorithmic steps are detailed below.

title: Bush Cat Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Bush Cat Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Bush Cat Algorithm (BCA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bush cats (scientific name: *Caracal caracal*). Bush cats are renowned for their efficient and adaptive hunting strategies, particularly their ability to locate prey amidst complex and fluctuating environments. The BCA mimics these behaviors through a combination of exploration and exploitation phases, utilizing a dynamic movement system and a novel prey-predator interaction mechanism. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The movement of individuals is governed by a stochastic process, influenced by environmental factors and the presence of "prey" (representing promising solutions). The BCA is designed to be adaptable and robust, with parameters that can be tuned to suit different optimization problems. Experimental results on benchmark functions demonstrate the effectiveness of the BCA in comparison to established metaheuristic algorithms like the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's performance is evaluated based on convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency. This research contributes a new optimization technique with potential applications in various fields, including engineering design, financial modeling, and machine learning.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的概率逻辑控制系统
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic control system based on an adaptive neural network (ANN). The system dynamically adjusts system parameters based on the input data's probability distribution, offering enhanced control and optimization capabilities compared to traditional approaches. We detail the architecture of the ANN, the learning algorithm employed, and the resulting improvements in performance and robustness. The core mechanism lies in the adaptive weighting of input data points, allowing the network to respond intelligently to changing conditions. The proposed system addresses limitations of existing control methodologies by providing a flexible and adaptable framework for complex systems. We provide a comprehensive analysis of the system's performance through simulation and initial experimental validation.

title: ## Bonda Mastiff Bat: A Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Bonda Mastiff Hunting Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a novel meta-heuristic optimization algorithm, Bonda Mastiff Bat (BMB), inspired by the hunting behavior of Bonda Mastiffs, a unique breed of dog known for its strategic and persistent hunting techniques. The algorithm leverages the Bonda Mastiff's ability to efficiently explore a search space by utilizing a combination of echo location, strategic flight patterns, and focused pursuit. BMB employs a population-based approach, simulating the bats' collective intelligence. The core components of the algorithm include a position update mechanism mimicking the bats' flight path, a memory update mechanism representing echo location, and a convergence criterion based on the bats' pursuit behavior. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. The key contributions of this work include a novel algorithm design grounded in a specific animal behavior, a detailed explanation of its underlying principles, and empirical validation of its capabilities. The algorithm's parameters are designed to offer a balance between exploration and exploitation, leading to robust performance across various optimization problems. Future research will focus on adapting the BMB algorithm to solve complex real-world problems.

title: Configuration of climatological limits for surface radiation measurement quality control: a global assessment using a novel radiation climate classification
abstract: Abstract. Quality control (QC) of ground-based solar radiation measurements is fundamental to ensuring the integrity of surface energy balance and climatological studies. The extremely rare limit (ERL) test, a widely implemented QC standard, is frequently noted for being overly conservative, often failing to isolate subtle instrumental or environmental anomalies. To improve QC tightness and sensitivity, this study presents a data-driven framework for configuring regime-specific climatological limits. Diverging from traditional climate classifications that do not directly account for radiative variability, we define seven distinct radiation regimes through unsupervised learning, utilizing principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering. For each identified regime, optimal test coefficients are established via a machine-learning-based optimization strategy. Specifically, we maximize the F1 score by benchmarking the climatological limit test against an isolation forest outlier detection model. Validation using global measurements from the Baseline Surface Radiation Network demonstrates that the proposed regional limits provide a significantly tighter fit to observed data distributions compared to the original global ERL thresholds. This methodology offers a scalable and automated approach to regionalizing QC procedures, substantially enhancing the precision of global radiation monitoring networks.

title: APPROACH-AVOIDANCE OPTIMIZATION ALGORITHM: A NOVEL METAPHOR-FREE OPTIMIZER WITH APPLICATIONS IN DATA CLUSTERING
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaphor-free optimization algorithm called Approach-Avoidance Optimization Algorithm (AAOA) to solve real-world optimization problems. AAOA is built on the principle that candidate solutions should move towards better solutions and away from worse ones. The algorithm utilizes an effective collective search strategy by enabling randomized variable-level information exchange among candidate solutions, thereby facilitating a comprehensive and efficient exploration of the search space. Due to its simplicity, ease of implementation, and parameter-free nature, AAOA is particularly suitable for users without deep expertise in optimization. The performance of AAOA was evaluated through extensive experiments on the CEC 2017 benchmark functions across various dimensions, as well as on 30 real-world data clustering problems. Its performance was compared against eight metaphor-free algorithms using different evaluation criteria. Experimental results demonstrated that AAOA achieved competitive or superior performance in most cases, highlighting its potential as a robust and practical tool for high-dimensional and complex optimization tasks. This study contributes to the growing body of research on simple yet effective optimization algorithms that do not rely on metaphorical analogies.

title: A Multi-Feature Radio-Frequency Framework for UAV Behavioral State Recognition and Prediction
abstract: Existing RF-based UAV detection methods achieve high accuracy in identifying UAV presence and model type, yet they largely characterize UAVs through static signal attributes, offering limited insight into what an identified UAV is actually doing. This gap constrains their practical value for airspace monitoring and threat assessment. This paper presents a multi-feature RF-based framework for UAV behavioral state recognition and short-horizon behavior prediction, built upon a set of newly defined behavioral indicators, namely, spectral dynamics, signal-power-based motion trend, and communication density, integrated through a dedicated time-series modeling module. To support this study, we construct UAV-BehaviorRF, a new dataset with fine-grained behavioral annotations collected via a scripted multi-state flight protocol across eight UAV models. Experiments on UAV-BehaviorRF and the public DroneRFa dataset show that the proposed framework achieves accurate behavioral state recognition and reliable state-transition prediction, while remaining robust under interference and real-world conditions and maintaining real-time processing suitable for resource-constrained deployment.

title: Sentiment Analysis of User Reviews of Purwokerto Station Using TF-IDF and the Random Forest Method
abstract: User reviews on Google Maps serve as a valuable source of information for evaluating the service quality of public facilities, including train stations. This study aims to analyze the sentiment of user reviews for Purwokerto Station using the Random Forest algorithm and to identify dominant Bigrams within each sentiment class to provide insights for station management. The dataset was obtained by scraping Google Maps, yielding 2,232 reviews after data cleaning. The research process involved sentiment labeling based on ratings; text preprocessing (cleaning, case folding, tokenization, non-standard word normalization, stopword removal, and single-token deduplication); and feature extraction using Bigram-based Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF–IDF). The dataset was split into 80% training data and 20% testing data, then classified using the Random Forest algorithm. Results indicate that the model achieved 90.16% accuracy on the test data. However, evaluation revealed that while the model excelled at recognizing the positive class, it struggled to identify negative and neutral classes; this was evidenced by a Macro F1-score of 0.32 and precision, recall, and F1-score values ​​of 0.00 for both the negative and neutral classes. This outcome was driven by an imbalanced data distribution, causing the model to lean toward predicting reviews as positive. Bigram analysis showed that the phrase "clean and comfortable" dominated positive sentiment, whereas phrases such as "waiting room" and "ticket counter staff" more frequently in negative sentiment. evidence.title: Sentiment Analysis of User Reviews of Purwokerto Station Using TF-IDF and the Random Forest Method
evidence.abstract: User reviews on Google Maps serve as a valuable source of information for evaluating the service quality of public facilities, including train stations. This study aims to analyze the sentiment of user reviews for Purwokerto Station using the Random Forest algorithm and to identify dominant Bigrams within each sentiment class to provide insights for station management. The dataset was obtained by scraping Google Maps, yielding 2,232 reviews after data cleaning. The research process involved sentiment labeling based on ratings; text preprocessing (cleaning, case folding, tokenization, non-standard word normalization, stopword removal, and single-token deduplication); and feature extraction using Bigram-based Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF–IDF). The dataset was split into 80% training data and 20% testing data, then classified using the Random Forest algorithm. Results indicate that the model achieved 90.16% accuracy on the test data. However, evaluation revealed that while the model excelled at recognizing the positive class, it struggled to identify negative and neutral classes; this was evidenced by a Macro F1-score of 0.32 and precision, recall, and F1-score values ​​of 0.00 for both the negative and neutral classes. This outcome was driven by an imbalanced data distribution, causing the model to lean toward predicting reviews as positive. Bigram analysis showed that the phrase "clean and comfortable" dominated positive sentiment, whereas phrases such as "waiting room" and "ticket counter staff" more frequently in negative sentiment. title: Evaluating Personal Information Output from Conversational Interactions in Generative AI Systems
abstract: This exploratory pilot study evaluates the scope and perceived accuracy of personal information output from ongoing conversational interactions in generative AI systems using GPT-5.2 Instant and GPT-5.2 Thinking, categorized into three output types: Fact, Inference, and Confidence. Based on the evaluation results obtained from 15 Japanese participants, differences in model design have limited impact on personal information output tendencies. Compared with the Inference type, the Fact type shows a more conservative output pattern. Regarding attribute categories, the findings indicate that Core Personal attributes associated with identification are treated relatively conservatively, whereas Behavioral and Linguistic attributes show higher accuracy across both Fact and Inference outputs. Furthermore, Holistic Profile, Psychological and Cognitive, and Residual attributes are more readily inferred, even when not supported by explicit factual outputs. Notably, the lack of null outputs for these attributes in the Inference type suggests that such inferred profiles may be constructed from indirectly available contextual information. The findings may contribute to future discussions regarding privacy awareness and personal information inference in generative AI systems.

title: Consistency as Regularization for Unsupervised Shadow Removal
abstract: Shadow removal is an important preprocessing step for many vision tasks, yet existing supervised methods require paired shadow and shadow-free images, while unsupervised approaches often still rely on shadow masks or shadow-free references. We propose ShadowCLR, an unsupervised framework that learns shadow removal directly from shadow images. Our key observation is that shadows vary across observations while the underlying scene content remains largely consistent. We therefore use consistency across shadow observations as regularization, encouraging the model to recover scene-consistent appearance while suppressing shadow-specific variations. Global and local consistency further enable us to explore visually related images, learn from imperfectly aligned observations, and focus the representation on shared scene information. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that ShadowCLR achieves competitive and often superior performance over state-of-the-art unsupervised methods, demonstrating that consistency can provide regularization for shadow removal without shadow masks or shadow-free images.

title: Gaussian Core LoRA: Distribution-Aware Dynamic Adaptation for Broad Concept Erasure
abstract: Concept erasure aims to suppress unsafe, privacy-sensitive, or undesirable generations in text-to-image diffusion models while preserving benign semantics, visual quality, and deployment efficiency. Existing adapter-based methods, such as Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), typically freeze the diffusion backbone and learn lightweight parameter updates to steer generation away from target semantics. However, these methods usually assign a static semantic erasure direction to each target concept. This assumption is overly coarse for broad and complex target concepts, since a concept often contains multiple latent semantic prototypes involving different objects, scenes, or relations, and requires different local erasure directions. A single LoRA update averages these heterogeneous erasure demands, leading to under-erasure on difficult prototypes and over-editing of nearby benign semantics. To address this limitation, we propose Gaussian Core LoRA, a distribution-aware low-rank adaptation framework. It fits a Gaussian mixture model in the prompt feature space to estimate latent semantic prototypes within the target concept. During inference, each input prompt is projected into this feature space to compute its Gaussian posterior responsibilities, which condition the core generator to produce a prompt-specific, norm-bounded residual reconfiguration of the shared LoRA rank space. This enables prototype-adaptive erasure with a single lightweight adapter. Compared with the strongest baseline on each metric, Gaussian Core LoRA reduces average Attack Success Rate (ASR) by 7.95%, lowers COCO Fr'echet Inception Distance (FID) by 14.72%, and improves CLIP Score by 4.98%. Further experiments show robustness to adversarial prompts, scalability to multi-identity and multi-style erasure, and compatibility with SDXL and FLUX.

title: On-the-Fly3R: Towards Robust Online 3D Reconstruction with Feed-Forward 3R Models for Large-Scale UAV Scenarios
abstract: While feed-forward 3D reconstruction (3R) offers efficient end-to-end modeling, its application in large-scale UAV mapping is hindered by the prohibitive memory cost of Transformer attention. Current scalable streaming 3R methods assume temporally and spatially continuous inputs, rendering them ineffective for the weakly ordered or unordered image streams common in cross-strip UAV operations. To address this, we propose On-the-Fly3R, a training-free, progressive online 3D reconstruction framework for large-scale UAV images that upgrades various 3R backbones for large-scale UAV scenarios. Our method enables reconstruction from unordered inputs via retrieval-guided dynamic subset construction, which adaptively selects spatially relevant images. To further improve the robustness, a validation-rejection-retry mechanism is designed to guarantee global consistency, performing a pre-integration consistency check and automatically rejecting misaligned images and retrying with alternative subset. Finally, inspired by VSLAM, pose graph optimization based on the retrieval loop closure is employed to mitigate camera drift. Evaluations on several UAV benchmarks show that our On-the-Fly3R successfully scales various 3R models to over 5,000 images across square-kilometer UAV scenes, delivering substantially superior accuracy compared to several SOTA streaming 3R methods. Code is available at https://github.com/Sh1nZzz/On_the_Fly3R

title: ADAPTIVE REPRESENTATION LEARNING FOR ROBUST ANOMALY DETECTION IN NON-STATIONARY MULTISOURCE DATA STREAMS
abstract: Abstract Anomaly detection in multisource data streams becomes substantially more difficult when the underlying data-generating process is non-stationary. A pattern considered abnormal at one time can become part of normal operation after a regime transition, while previously typical observations can acquire anomalous significance under changed system conditions. Simultaneously, heterogeneous sources may differ in temporal resolution, noise structure, feature dimensionality, missingness, reliability, and semantic content. Static anomaly detectors trained on a fixed historical distribution therefore tend to lose calibration as both representation and decision boundaries become obsolete. This study develops a conceptual framework for adaptive representation learning aimed at robust anomaly detection in non-stationary multisource streams. The analysis distinguishes genuine anomalies from concept drift, recurrent regimes, transient disturbances, sensor degradation, and source-specific distribution shifts. Representation learning is treated as a dynamic process in which latent features must preserve anomaly-relevant information while adapting selectively to legitimate evolution of normal behaviour. Classical anomaly-detection principles establish the importance of defining normality relative to context rather than relying solely on global rarity [1]. Concept-drift research further demonstrates that online learning systems require explicit mechanisms for detecting and responding to changes in the underlying distribution [2]. Adaptive windows provide one practical means of controlling the temporal horizon over which current behaviour is estimated [3]. For multisource environments, additional challenges arise from asynchronous observations and unequal source reliability, requiring representation architectures that can integrate shared information without suppressing source-specific anomalies. Robust adaptation is therefore formulated as a balance among memory, plasticity, contamination resistance, and uncertainty. Deep and shallow anomaly-detection paradigms are considered jointly, with particular attention to latent-space stability, reconstruction-based scoring, support estimation, and adaptive thresholding.

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A Critical Survey Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Adaptive Probabilistic Graphical Model Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to learning probabilistic graphical models (PGMs) by dynamically adapting their structure based on the underlying data distribution. Traditional PGM learning often relies on pre-defined structures, which may not always capture the intricate relationships present in complex datasets. Our method, Adaptive Probabilistic Graphical Model Learning (APGML), leverages Bayesian inference and variational inference techniques, coupled with gradient descent optimization, to automatically adjust the model's topology – specifically, the nodes and edges – during the learning process. The core claim is that this adaptive approach leads to a more precise representation of the data and improved model accuracy. We introduce a framework that iteratively refines the PGM structure, driven by the data, ultimately resulting in a model that better reflects the underlying dependencies. This work addresses a significant challenge in PGM learning: the selection of an appropriate graph structure – a problem often tackled through manual design or heuristic search algorithms – by allowing the model to evolve based on the observed data. We outline the key components of the APGML algorithm, including the variational inference process, the structural adaptation mechanism, and the optimization strategy.

title: Quantum Topology for Adaptive Quantum Computation Validation
abstract: Quantum topology, a novel field of physics, offers a unique framework for validating quantum computations. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum topology to dynamically adjust parameters within a quantum computing algorithm, thereby enhancing computational accuracy and stability. We introduce a novel self-adaptive validation framework based on topological invariants, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary results. The core mechanism involves quantifying the system's topological properties and using this information to iteratively refine quantum parameter adjustments, ensuring a robust and reliable computation. This work represents a significant step toward automated quantum verification, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum algorithm development and error mitigation.

title: ## Central Andes Thomasomys: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Behavioral Adaptations
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the "Thomasomys Adaptation Algorithm" (TAA), inspired by the behavioral adaptations observed in *Thomasomys* rodents of the Central Andes. These rodents exhibit remarkable foraging strategies and navigation skills within complex, unpredictable environments. The TAA leverages these observed behaviors – particularly the dynamic adjustment of search strategies based on environmental feedback – to construct a robust and efficient optimization process. The algorithm incorporates elements of adaptive step size control, dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, and a novel representation of the solution space based on a weighted sum of heuristic indicators derived from the observed rodent behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the TAA through simulations targeting several benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that the TAA performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms, showcasing its potential for tackling challenging optimization tasks where adaptability and environmental awareness are crucial. The key innovations of the TAA lie in its biologically-inspired approach and the ability to dynamically adjust its search parameters based on the perceived success of previous iterations. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of problem types, including continuous, discrete, and combinatorial optimization.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Feature Selection for High-Dimensional Data
abstract: Quantum-enhanced feature selection is a promising approach to address the challenges posed by high-dimensional data in machine learning. Traditional feature selection methods often struggle to effectively identify the most informative features, leading to suboptimal model performance and increased computational cost. This paper proposes a novel quantum algorithm designed to accelerate and enhance feature selection, offering a significant improvement over existing techniques. We explore the potential of quantum algorithms, specifically focusing on Grover's search algorithm and quantum-enhanced k-means clustering, to achieve efficient identification of relevant features. The core mechanism involves exploiting quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to enhance the search space and improve the selection process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing its potential to reduce computational cost and improve accuracy in high-dimensional feature selection scenarios.

title: Self-Organizing Maps for Anomaly Detection in Streaming Data
abstract: This paper explores the application of Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) for anomaly detection within streaming data environments. The primary challenge in anomaly detection lies in the scarcity of labeled data, a common issue when dealing with continuous data streams. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing SOMs to autonomously learn the normal patterns within the stream. Anomalies are then identified by quantifying the deviation of incoming data points from their closest representation on the learned SOM map. The core of the method centers around the distance metric between data points and their nearest neighbors on the map. This approach offers a viable solution for real-time anomaly detection without requiring pre-labeled datasets. The effectiveness of this methodology is demonstrated through a theoretical framework and conceptual outline, highlighting its potential for diverse streaming data applications.

title: Title: Adaptive Information Theory for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum information processing is exceptionally sensitive to errors, posing a significant challenge to the development of practical quantum technologies. Conventional error correction codes, while effective, often rely on pre-defined error profiles that may not accurately represent the true error distribution within a quantum system. This research investigates an adaptive information theory framework designed to dynamically adjust error correction parameters based on the specific error profile of the quantum system, thereby improving error detection and resilience. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors the error rate and optimizes the correction parameters to minimize the impact of errors. The proposed approach offers a more flexible and potentially superior solution compared to static error correction methods, addressing a key limitation in current quantum error correction strategies. This work explores the design of a novel system that can adapt to varying error characteristics, leading to enhanced robustness and improved performance in quantum information processing.

title: Self-Adaptive Neural Network Control Algorithm
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of a novel self-adaptive neural network control algorithm. Traditional neural networks often rely on fixed parameters, rendering them inadequate for dynamic systems. This research proposes a method leveraging the inherent self-adaptivity of neural networks to dynamically adjust network weights, thereby optimizing system performance and stability. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously assesses the system's state and adjusts the network's weights in response, ensuring optimal performance. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, parameterization, and validation through a series of simulations and experiments. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in performance metrics compared to conventional control strategies.

title: Quantum-Inspired Randomized Response for Privacy-Preserving Data Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to privacy-preserving data analysis termed Quantum-Inspired Randomized Response (QIRR). Traditional privacy-preserving techniques, such as differential privacy and homomorphic encryption, frequently necessitate substantial computational resources, presenting limitations in scalability and real-time applications. QIRR leverages concepts derived from quantum measurement theory – specifically, the probabilistic collapse phenomenon – to provide a computationally efficient solution. The core principle involves a randomized response strategy where an individual answers a query in a way that obscures their true response, while still allowing for aggregate analysis. We formalize this approach with a mathematical framework, outlining the key parameters and processes involved. The system is designed to minimize computational overhead, offering a practical alternative to existing methods. This work demonstrates a viable pathway for integrating quantum-inspired ideas into data privacy, potentially enabling more accessible and scalable privacy-preserving analytics. The system utilizes a Bernoulli distribution to model the randomization process, and the final result is derived through weighted averaging based on the responses. We explore the impact of varying parameters on privacy guarantees and analytical accuracy.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Evolutionary Algorithms (QEAs) represent a novel approach to optimization, aiming to significantly accelerate the evolution of complex, high-dimensional evolutionary algorithms. This paper explores the potential of quantum mechanics to enhance the optimization process, focusing on leveraging quantum properties such as superposition and entanglement to accelerate exploration of the search space and improve convergence. We detail the core mechanism of QEAs, outlining the key design choices and theoretical underpinnings. The paper argues that the integration of quantum elements can provide a substantial performance advantage over classical approaches, particularly for problems exhibiting complex, high-dimensional landscapes. The research will demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary analysis, emphasizing the potential for enhanced search efficiency and robustness.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Causal Reasoning
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have achieved significant success in representing graph structures for various downstream tasks. However, a critical limitation of current approaches is their inability to effectively model the temporal dynamics inherent in evolving graphs. This paper introduces a novel framework for temporal graph embedding that explicitly incorporates causal reasoning. We propose a method that combines standard graph structure with a causal Bayesian network representation, allowing us to learn node embeddings that maximize the likelihood of observed graph transitions, given the learned causal model. This approach enables the representation of temporal dependencies and facilitates reasoning about "what-if" scenarios, addressing a fundamental gap in existing graph embedding methodologies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a simplified example.

title: ## Blaubok: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Blaubok*
abstract: This paper presents Blaubok, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Blaubok* (a hypothetical, social insect-like creature). *Blaubok* exhibits a unique strategy of collaborative exploration and localized decision-making within a group, followed by periodic aggregation and information sharing. Blaubok leverages these principles to develop a new algorithm, Blaubok-Metaheuristic, designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates a population-based search, a novel communication mechanism simulating *Blaubok's* aggregation behavior, and a dynamic adjustment of individual exploration and exploitation strategies based on the aggregated information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Blaubok-Metaheuristic on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function, showcasing its competitive performance against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that Blaubok-Metaheuristic offers a robust and adaptable approach to tackling challenging optimization tasks.

title: Black-tailed Gerbil Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Black-tailed Gerbil Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Black-tailed Gerbil Algorithm (BTGA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Gerbillus clanianus*, commonly known as the black-tailed gerbil. Gerbils exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating food sources in complex environments, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies. BTGA mimics these behaviors through a novel population-based search process incorporating adaptive movement patterns, resource assessment, and social learning. The algorithm employs a dynamic agent representation, where each agent simulates a gerbil exploring the search space. Agents' movement is governed by a stochastic rule based on environmental cues and their own past experiences. Resource assessment is performed using a weighted average of local neighborhood evaluations. Social learning is implemented through a mechanism where agents preferentially adopt movements from successful neighbors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BTGA on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and Brent's patuitary function. The results indicate that BTGA achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in problems with complex landscapes and high dimensionality. The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising candidate for various optimization challenges.

title: Training Without Gathering the Data: A Historical Development Review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of federated learning and privacy as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Process of Marketing Management in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
abstract: Purpose: The primary objective of this study was to determine how the use of artificial intelligence tools affects the efficiency of marketing management in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Poland, based on original research.To achieve this objective, the study identified the marketing areas where artificial intelligence (AI) is most frequently employed, assessed entrepreneurs' awareness and knowledge regarding AI, analyzed the benefits, barriers, and limitations associated with its implementation, evaluated the impact of AI usage on operational efficiency, and outlined prospects for future development.Design/Methodology/Approach: This study employs a survey-based research method using a questionnaire.The questionnaire was designed to gather information on the extent to which enterprises use artificial intelligence tools in their marketing activities, the assessment of their effectiveness, the marketing areas supported by AI technologies, and the barriers and challenges associated with implementing these solutions in practice.Findings: The results clearly indicate that AI is no longer merely an experimental technology but has become one of the most common optimization tools.High levels of awareness and implementation of AI tools within enterprises were also observed.SME managers view AI as a key element in building a competitive advantage, enabling them to bridge the resource gap vis-à-vis large corporations.The dominant model of AI adoption is task automation.The popularity of using AI for content creation, managing marketing campaigns, and data analysis suggests that the technology is viewed primarily as a tool for automating tasks.The main benefit for organizations is not a direct reduction in financial costs-in this regard, the gains for the enterprise are usually negligible or minor.However, the radical optimization of working time is the primary driver behind the popularity of AI tools.Current trends in how these tools are implemented within enterprises suggest that the approach to human resource utilization may undergo a significant shift in the coming years, with a growing trend of moving personnel away from routine tasks toward conceptual or strategic activities.Practical Implications: Leveraging AI in marketing management within SMEs significantly boosts effectiveness and improves overall business performance.However, success in this area will increasingly depend not merely on the technology itself, but on the organization's ability to adapt and educate itself in order to avoid falling behind in the digital landscape.

title: Machine learning-enhanced modified early warning system for predicting in-hospital mortality on pulmonary ward
abstract: Background: Early recognition of impending systemic failure and timely delivery of appropriate medical care are critical for effective clinical intervention. The Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS) is widely used to identify patients at risk of clinical deterioration. However, as patient complexity increases—driven by advanced age, multimorbidity, and other risk factors—automated warning systems often generate excessive alerts, leading to high false-alarm rates. Therefore, we aim to develop and validate a machine learning-enhanced predictive model (MEWS+) to detect critical in-hospital mortality risk factors earlier, thereby supporting clinical decision-making and optimizing acute care triage on pulmonary wards. Methods: This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from 4,108 consecutive adult patients admitted to the pulmonary wards of a medical center between January and June 2021. Four machine learning (ML) frameworks—extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forest, logistic regression, and support vector machine—were trained and evaluated using an 80:20 data split. Pairwise nonparametric Spearman rank correlation was used to assess associations between baseline predictors and in-hospital mortality. Results: Among the 4,108 patients included, the cohort was predominantly elderly (60.6% aged ≥65 years) and female (61.6%), with males accounting for 38.4%. The baseline in-hospital mortality rate was 5.4%, representing 222 empirical mortality events. Spearman correlation analysis showed that the recalculated traditional MEWS score had the strongest positive monotonic association with in-hospital mortality (ρs =0.430, P<0.05), followed by signed do-not-resuscitate (DNR) status (ρs =0.383, P<0.05), MEWS time (ρs =0.292, P<0.05), and age (ρs =0.204, P<0.05). In contrast, chronic comorbidities demonstrated very weak correlations (heart failure: ρs =0.079; hypertension: ρs =0.035). On the independent testing set, the XGBoost classifier achieved the highest predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.970 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.944–0.990], sensitivity of 0.872 (95% CI: 0.743–0.952), and specificity of 0.972 (95% CI: 0.957–0.982). Feature-importance analysis indicated that the MEWS score (0.402), signed DNR status (0.194), and MEWS time (0.136) were the primary contributors to model performance. Conclusions: An ML-enhanced MEWS+ model by effectively balancing clinical sensitivity and operational precision, by integrating acute physiological indicators with advanced directives and demographic factors, the XGBoost-based MEWS+ system provides highly accurate, individualized early-warning triage to strengthen clinical safety on general hospital wards.

title: Thought-Mediated Learning: From Deliberative Reasoning to Automatic Behavior
abstract: Autonomous agents require not only deliberate reasoning for unfamiliar situations but also the ability to convert repeatedly useful reasoning into efficient automatic behavior. However, existing LLM-based agents and knowledge-distillation approaches generally couple reasoning and learning through predefined training objectives or direct teacher--student supervision, leaving unclear how an agent can autonomously determine what should become learned behavior. This paper proposes Thought-Mediated Learning (TML), a framework that separates LLM-based deliberative thinking from an independent ML/DL background learning process. Thinking cannot directly update the automatic model; instead, it produces thought materials whose content and frequency determine what becomes available for learning. Repeated thinking implicitly strengthens important experiences, attention determines which factors are represented, jointly considered events may create spurious associations, and imagined experiences can provide learning materials before corresponding real events occur. Observed outcomes further generate corrective materials that revise previously learned automatic behavior. Experimental results show that TML achieves 96.67% hidden-pattern acquisition and 99.93% post-learning automatic accuracy, reaches 97.83% OOD (out-of-distribution) accuracy versus 9.50% for raw learning, and improves zero-real rare-case success to 59.38% while corrective learning raises final hidden-case success to 96.82%.

title: Συστηματική υποβοήθηση νεοφυών επιχειρήσεων με χρήση τεχνικών τεχνητής νοημοσύνης
abstract: Η παρούσα διδακτορική διατριβή εξετάζει το πρόβλημα της συστηματικής υποβοήθησης και αξιολόγησης νεοφυών επιχειρήσεων (startups) με τη χρήση τεχνικών Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης. Οι νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις πρώιμου σταδίου (early stage startups) λειτουργούν υπό συνθήκες αυξημένης αβεβαιότητας, περιορισμένων οικονομικών και ανθρώπινων πόρων και άνισης πρόσβασης σε εξειδικευμένη καθοδήγηση. Οι παραδοσιακοί μηχανισμοί υποστήριξης, όπως οι σύμβουλοι, οι θερμοκοιτίδες και οι επιταχυντές, παρέχουν σημαντική εμπειρογνωμοσύνη, αλλά περιορίζονται ως προς το κόστος, τη διαθεσιμότητα και τη δυνατότητα κλιμάκωσης. Παράλληλα όμως, η διάδοση της Παραγωγικής Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης και των Μεγάλων Γλωσσικών Μοντέλων (LLMs) δημιουργεί αναντίλεκτα νέες δυνατότητες για παροχή καθοδήγησης κατά απαίτηση, χωρίς όμως να επιλύει αυτομάτως το πρόβλημα. Η χρήση μοντέλων γενικού σκοπού (LLMs) σε ρόλο συμβούλου ή αυτόνομου αξιολογητή συνοδεύεται, λόγω του τρόπου λειτουργίας τους, από παραισθήσεις (hallucinations), εξάρτηση από στατικά δεδομένα, τάση συγκατάβασης προς τις υποθέσεις του χρήστη (sycophancy), αστάθεια της βαθμολόγησης και περιορισμένη προσαρμογή τόσο στο στάδιο ανάπτυξης όσο και στο επιχειρηματικό πλαίσιο κάθε startup. Σκοπός της διατριβής είναι ο σχεδιασμός, η υλοποίηση και η εμπειρική αξιολόγηση ενός ολοκληρωμένου υπολογιστικού τεχνουργήματος, του Evaluator.GR, το οποίο υποστηρίζει συστηματικά τη διαδρομή μιας νεοφυούς επιχείρησης από τη διαμόρφωση και την επικύρωση της αρχικής ιδέας έως την προετοιμασία για χρηματοδότηση και την επενδυτική ετοιμότητα. Η έρευνα δεν αντιμετωπίζει την Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη ως συνολικό υποκατάστατο του ανθρώπινου μέντορα, αξιολογητή ή επενδυτή, αλλά ως υποδομή υποστήριξης της ανθρώπινης κρίσης και αυτοματοποίησης επιμέρους εργασιών, με έμφαση στην αξιοπιστία, στην τεκμηρίωση, στην επεξηγησιμότητα και στην υπεύθυνη χρήση. Ως κύριο μεθοδολογικό πλαίσιο υιοθετήθηκε η Έρευνα Επιστήμης Σχεδιασμού (Design Science Research), μέσω των αλληλοτροφοδοτούμενων Κύκλων Συνάφειας, Σχεδιασμού και Αυστηρότητας. Στον Κύκλο Συνάφειας πραγματοποιήθηκε Συστηματική Ταχεία Αξιολόγηση Τεκμηρίων, η οποία χαρτογράφησε τις εφαρμογές, τις συνθήκες απόδοσης και τους περιορισμούς της Παραγωγικής Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης (generative AI) στην καθοδήγηση και αξιολόγηση startups. Τα αναγνωρισμένα ερευνητικά κενά μετασχηματίστηκαν, στον Κύκλο Σχεδιασμού, σε λειτουργικές και αρχιτεκτονικές απαιτήσεις του Evaluator.GR. Στον Κύκλο Αυστηρότητας, το τεχνούργημα αξιολογήθηκε μέσω συγκριτικής μελέτης έναντι μοντέλων γενικού σκοπού και μέσω πιλοτικής εφαρμογής σε πραγματικές νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις.Το υπολογιστικό τεχνούργημα (artifact) που αναπτύχθηκε είναι το Evaluator.GR, μια πολυαρθρωτή πλατφόρμα αξιολόγησης, στρατηγικής υποστήριξης και παραγωγής επιχειρηματικών παραδοτέων. Η αρχιτεκτονική του συνδυάζει Μίξη Ειδικών σε επίπεδο συστήματος (System-Level Mixture of Experts), τριπλό αξιολογητή και επιπροσθέτως μηχανισμό Μετα-Αξιολογητή (Meta-Judge). Παράλληλα όμως, χρησιμοποιεί σταδιο-προσαρμοστικές ρουμπρίκες (rubrics), παραγωγή με ενίσχυση ανάκτησης (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) και αναζήτηση στον Παγκόσμιο Ιστό (world wide web). Η ανθρώπινη εποπτεία ενσωματώνεται λοιπόν σε τρία (3) επίπεδα. Οι μηχανισμοί αυτοί σχεδιάστηκαν ώστε να περιορίζουν την εξάρτηση από έναν μεμονωμένο LLM γενικού σκοπού, να ενισχύουν τη γείωση και την τεκμηρίωση των αποτελεσμάτων και να διατηρούν την τελική ευθύνη στον άνθρωπο. Παράλληλα, η πλατφόρμα αναπτύχθηκε με αρχές Συμμόρφωσης βάσει Σχεδιασμού, σε ευθυγράμμιση με το EU AI Act και το NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Τα δεδομένα αξιολόγησης προήλθαν από τρεις συμπληρωματικές πηγές. Η Συστηματική Ταχεία Αξιολόγηση Τεκμηρίων περιέλαβε τριάντα τέσσερα (34) τελικά τεκμήρια της περιόδου 2022–2025. Η συγκριτική μελέτη πραγματοποιήθηκε με 139 αξιολογητές, 52 στην ελληνόφωνη και 87 στην αγγλόφωνη ομάδα, οι οποίοι αξιολόγησαν το Evaluator.GR, το Gemini 3 και το ChatGPT 5.2 σε δεκατέσσερις (14) διαστάσεις. Επιπλέον, υλοποιήθηκε πιλοτική εφαρμογή διάρκειας 30 ημερών με 10 νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις στα στάδια Pre-seed και Seed. Στη συγκριτική αξιολόγηση, το Evaluator.GR έλαβε συνολικό μέσο όρο 4,51/5, έναντι 3,64/5 για το Gemini 3 και 2,37/5 για το ChatGPT 5.2. Τα ποιοτικά ευρήματα του πιλοτικού προγράμματος έδειξαν ότι το σύστημα μπορούσε να εντοπίζει ουσιώδεις επιχειρηματικές ή τεχνικές αδυναμίες και να παρέχει προσαρμοσμένες συστάσεις, ανέδειξαν όμως και περιπτώσεις στις οποίες απαιτήθηκαν ανθρώπινη παρέμβαση, επανεξέταση ή βαθμονόμηση των αποτελεσμάτων. Η συνεισφορά της διατριβής είναι θεωρητική, μεθοδολογική, τεχνική και πρακτική. Συνδέει τη βιβλιογραφία για την υποστήριξη startups με GenAI, το LLM-as-a-judge και την Υπεύθυνη Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη (Responsible AI) με το πλαίσιο Mentor–Evaluator Stack, ενσωματώνει τη βιβλιογραφική σύνθεση, την κατασκευή και την εμπειρική αξιολόγηση στο πλαίσιο της DSR και προτείνει μια πολυπρακτορική, σταδιο-προσαρμοστική και ελεγχόμενη αρχιτεκτονική υποστήριξης της ανθρώπινης κρίσης. Τα αποτελέσματα, ωστόσο, αφορούν την αντιλαμβανόμενη ποιότητα, χρησιμότητα και αξιοπιστία στο συγκεκριμένο πλαίσιο αξιολόγησης. Δεν τεκμηριώνουν αιτιώδη επίδραση στη χρηματοδότηση, στην επιβίωση ή στη μακροχρόνια ανάπτυξη των startups. Πρόσθετοι περιορισμοί είναι η μικρή διάρκεια και κλίμακα του πιλοτικού προγράμματος, η εξάρτηση από συγκεκριμένες εκδόσεις μοντέλων, ρουμπρίκες και διαθέσιμα δεδομένα, καθώς και η λειτουργική επιβάρυνση που εισάγουν οι μηχανισμοί ανθρώπινης εποπτείας.

title: Enhancing retrieval-augmented generation via domain-adaptive embedding optimization: a unified fine-tuning strategy
abstract: With the growing adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) in diverse fields, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a pivotal paradigm to mitigate hallucinations and knowledge obsolescence. However, generic embedding models often falter when applied to vertical domains, suffering from a domain gap that compromises retrieval accuracy. This paper proposes a domain-adaptive embedding optimization scheme based on a Unified Fine-Tuning strategy. Furthermore, addressing the challenge of data scarcity in specialized fields, we introduce a novel dataset construction pipeline utilizing LLMs for data augmentation and hard negative mining. By leveraging this high-quality contrastive data and specialized loss functions, our approach synergistically optimizes retrieval recall and ranking precision within a single-stage bi-encoder architecture. Empirical results on vertical domain datasets demonstrate that our solution significantly outperforms baselines, particularly in the medical domain, improving MRR@10 and NDCG@10 by 3.4% and 2.7%, respectively. This study provides a concise, cost-effective, and architecturally efficient path for adapting RAG systems to specialized industrial contexts.
